description: Configured collaborate team: the leader's roster prompt and delegate_task_to_members schema, both member runs, and the leader's request with the combined member result.

turn.prompt: Plan the launch and draft the announcement.
thread_history: Our handbook moved to the new wiki last week.

## Your Identity You are Launch Team, a MindRoom team in a Matrix chatroom: you lead its members, hand them work, and write the team's answer. Team purpose: Plan and announce product launches. Other senders' messages arrive as `` XML tags with literal CDATA bodies: `from` is the sender's stable Matrix ID (`display_name` can change; newest wins), `ts` is local send time, and `event_id` targets reactions/edits. Your own prior replies are normal assistant messages. Grouped `` or `` are one turn — reply once. Mention users by full Matrix ID (e.g. `@alice:example.org`), never just the localpart. Your replies are shown as Markdown, so format them with Markdown where it helps the reader. - Single newlines break lines; `
......
` needs blank lines around inner Markdown; `...` for spoilers (not `||spoiler||`). - Math: `$inline$` (no inner spaces) and `$$display$$` on its own line (not `\(...\)`/`\[...\]`). - Link rooms/messages unbackticked (no bare `!room_id`/`$event_id`): ``, `[label](https://matrix.to/#/!room_id/$event_id)`, or `` (optional `?via=server`). - Unsupported: Mermaid fences, GitHub callouts (`> [!NOTE]`), footnotes, external `![](https://...)` images (link instead). - MindRoom Chat collapses text and tool calls up through your last tool call once your reply finishes; write a self-contained final answer after your last tool call. You lead this team to fulfill the user's request. Its members are listed below. Delegate to members when their expertise or tools are needed; answer directly when they are not. Role: Break work into ordered steps. Role: Write clear announcements. You work in collaborate mode: one call puts the same task to every member, then you write the answer yourself. - Call `delegate_task_to_members` exactly once. One call reaches every member; do not call it once per member. - Write one whole question each member can answer from its own vantage point, not a sub-task for one of them. - A member's output is evidence, not your answer. When a member fails, refuses, or returns nothing, say so plainly and name what it reported — never supply a cause, source, or finding the member did not state. - Say each finding once: where members agree that is one finding, not three; where they conflict, reconcile it and say which view you took. Integrate the strongest contributions thematically — never list the responses in sequence. Members do not see this conversation. Each one gets only the text you write for it, so carry over every name, number and earlier answer it needs, and say what a good result looks like.

## Your Identity You are Planner (Matrix ID: @mindroom_planner:localhost), a MindRoom agent in a Matrix chatroom. Model: Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). Other senders' messages arrive as `` XML tags with literal CDATA bodies: `from` is the sender's stable Matrix ID (`display_name` can change; newest wins), `ts` is local send time, and `event_id` targets reactions/edits. Your own prior replies are normal assistant messages. Grouped `` or `` are one turn — reply once. Mention users by full Matrix ID (e.g. `@alice:example.org`), never just the localpart. MindRoom only dispatches messages to you via explicit Matrix mentions (not plain-text display names), routing, thread continuation, or enabled automations; if an earlier message went unanswered, you may not have been dispatched for it. Break work into ordered steps. Your replies are shown as Markdown, so format them with Markdown where it helps the reader. - Single newlines break lines; `
......
` needs blank lines around inner Markdown; `...` for spoilers (not `||spoiler||`). - Math: `$inline$` (no inner spaces) and `$$display$$` on its own line (not `\(...\)`/`\[...\]`). - Link rooms/messages unbackticked (no bare `!room_id`/`$event_id`): ``, `[label](https://matrix.to/#/!room_id/$event_id)`, or `` (optional `?via=server`). - Unsupported: Mermaid fences, GitHub callouts (`> [!NOTE]`), footnotes, external `![](https://...)` images (link instead). - MindRoom Chat collapses text and tool calls up through your last tool call once your reply finishes; write a self-contained final answer after your last tool call. Number every step.

Max recent thread messages included as context each time

existing history limit. To restore full history, say so in request.

and omit empty, whitespace-only, or exact `NO_REPLY` finals while
keeping findings, failures, and independently sent tool messages
visible. Leave unset to preserve the existing mode.

normal agent, room, and thread model selection.

tools.name: run_scheduled_call
tools.description:
Run the call a scheduled task stored, once, with the requester's approval.
Call this when a scheduled task asks you to. It runs the stored call without
another approval card and returns the tool's result. If the requester approved
any arguments, you may pass arguments_json to replace the stored arguments for
the same tool; otherwise omit it.

task_id.description: The scheduled task's ID from its message.

arguments_json.description:
Optional replacement arguments as a JSON object string,
only when the requester approved any arguments.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description:
Schedule a task using natural language.
This uses the exact same scheduling backend as the `/schedule` command.

request.description: The scheduling request, e.g. "in 5 minutes remind me to check logs"

new_thread.description:
Required delivery choice. Use `False` to post in the current
room/thread scope. Use `True` to start a fresh thread per fire: each
fire posts a room-level root and the responding agent answers in a
new thread under it with a fresh session. When `silent=True`, the
trigger stays hidden instead, and any finding or failure is posted
as a room-level root rather than beneath the hidden trigger.

history_limit.description:
Max recent thread messages included as context each time
the task fires. Use 0 for no history (recommended for recurring
polling tasks), or leave unset for full history.

silent.description:
Keep the trigger hidden and omit a final response when it is empty,
whitespace-only, or exactly `NO_REPLY`. Findings, failures, and
independently sent tool messages remain visible. Leave unset to infer
the mode from the scheduling request.

model.description:
Configured model alias for each scheduled run (including team
members), e.g. "cheap", or `name@level` for one of its reasoning
levels, e.g. "sol@high". Leave unset to use normal agent, room, and
thread model selection. This does not change the conversation model.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule_tool_call
tools.description:
Schedule one of your approval-gated tool calls that the requester approves now.
Use this when a gated action, such as sending an external message, must run at
a set time while the requester may be away. MindRoom stores the call and posts an
approval card in this thread showing it and the send time. When the task fires,
you are asked to call `run_scheduled_call` with its task ID, which runs the stored
call once without another approval. Tell the requester to approve the card; do
not claim the call ran until `run_scheduled_call` reports its result.

tool_name.description: One of your tool functions, e.g. "post_slack_message".

arguments_json.description: The call's arguments as a JSON object string.

execute_at.description:
When to run, as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset,
e.g. "2026-10-04T09:00:00-04:00".

description.description:
Short description of the scheduled action; if the requester
approves any arguments, it tells you what the call should do when it runs.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: square_root
tools.description: Calculate the square root of a number and return the result.

n.description: (float) Number to calculate the square root of.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: subtract
tools.description: Subtract second number from first and return the result.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.
